items.raw_excerpt: Walk down almost any market street in Bangkok and someone will offer to paint a tattoo on your arm in under ten minutes. It looks convincing for about a week, fades a little more with every shower, and is gone before your next paycheque.

items.raw_excerpt: A British Columbia Supreme Court judge has ruled in favour of two harm-reduction activists convicted of drug trafficking who argued they were doing it to reduce the harms caused by toxic drugs.
items.summary_en: A judge in British Columbia has thrown out drug trafficking convictions for two men who ran a compassion club. This club gave drug users a safe place to use and test drugs. items.summary_en: Bill Delzell has spent four years trying to find the photographer who took pictures of San Francisco in the 1960s. He sent 75 unopened rolls of film to a small photo shop in Saskatchewan. The shop will develop the film so he can see what the pictures show.

items.raw_excerpt: Activists urge against reviving Niyamgiri bauxite mining, highlighting tribal rights, sacred lands, and legal safeguards against Vedanta-backed projects.
items.summary_en: Groups in Odisha are asking people to reject plans to restart bauxite mining in the Niyamgiri hills. They say the mountain is sacred land for tribal people and that mining could weaken legal protection for them. They also warn about mining projects backed by the large company Vedanta.
